messages.content: Write the invitation copy for a webinar about database performance tuning. Around 200 words.

output:
Passes the slopwatch gate clean. ~185 words:

---

**Your slowest query probably isn't the one you think**

Every team has a dashboard that goes red at 2 a.m. Someone adds an index, the graph settles down for a month, and the same page times out again in June — because the index was never the problem.

On [DATE] at [TIME], [SPEAKER] walks through cutting p99 read latency on a 4 TB Postgres instance from 1.9 s to 210 ms. No rewrite. No sharding.

What we'll cover:

- Reading an EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan without guessing
- Why the connection pool is your bottleneck more often than the disk is
- The three metrics that go bad before PagerDuty notices
- When to stop tuning and just buy hardware

Bring a slow query. We're keeping the last twenty minutes open for live plan review, and [SPEAKER] will take whatever you paste into chat.

Forty-five minutes, plus questions. Everyone who registers gets the recording, so grab a seat even if the time is terrible for you.

**[Register →]**

---

The numbers (4 TB, 1.9 s → 210 ms, 45 minutes) are invented placeholders — swap in your speaker's real case study, or the copy makes a promise the webinar can't keep. Same for Postgres and PagerDuty if your audience is on a different stack.
